package_info.package_manager: self-hosted (not a package manager, but a software platform)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of GitLab contain critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-7028 and CVE-2023-5356) that allow attackers to reset user passwords to unverified email addresses and abuse integrations to execute commands as other users, enabling account takeover and privilege escalation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends a password reset email to an unverified email address provided by the attacker, allowing them to receive the reset link and take over the account.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sending sensitive password reset links to unverified or attacker-controlled email addresses enables account takeover.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to send password reset emails only to previously verified addresses associated with the user account.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Password reset emails are legitimately sent to verified user emails during account recovery.
key_indicators: Password reset emails sent to unverified or new email addresses
Lack of verification step before sending sensitive emails

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code allows a user to execute slash commands via Slack/Mattermost integrations as another user, enabling privilege escalation or unauthorized actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing users to execute commands as other users without proper authorization enables privilege escalation and impersonation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to restrict command execution to the authenticated user who initiated the integration event.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate integrations execute commands only on behalf of the authenticated user.
key_indicators: Execution of commands as arbitrary users
Lack of user identity validation in integration logic

attack_chain.action: Attacker initiates a password reset for a target account, specifying an attacker-controlled email address.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives password reset link and takes over the account.

attack_chain.action: Attacker abuses Slack/Mattermost integration to execute slash commands as another user.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized access or escalates privileges within the GitLab instance.

behavioral_signatures: Password reset emails sent to unverified or new email addresses
Integration events resulting in command execution as users other than the initiator
file_indicators: Unusual modifications to password reset logic
Integration configuration changes allowing user impersonation
network_indicators: Outbound emails to addresses not previously associated with user accounts
Integration API calls with mismatched user identities
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor password reset events for emails sent to unverified or new addresses. Audit integration logs for commands executed as users other than the authenticated initiator. Alert on configuration changes to password reset and integration logic. Review outbound email logs and integration API activity for anomalies.
